subject: Private VPC: segmentation, control-plane proxying, and deployment checklist
messages:
From: James Miller <james.miller@acme-fin.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: infra@acme-fin.com
Date: 2027-05-12T15:24:00-07:00
Subject: Private deployment feasibility + control plane separation

Hi Evelyn,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We have a serious compliance requirement to run inference inside our VPC and, for some workloads, entirely on-prem in an air-gapped VLAN. Before we move to a PO, can you confirm if Redwood supports the following at a high level: 

- Control plane hosted by Redwood but with no inbound access into our VPC; outbound-only egress from a small set of control-plane IPs (we need static egress IPs or a proxy pattern).
- Data plane (model execution) that either runs on an edge pool you manage in our account or on our on-prem GPU cluster with a Redwood runtime.
- Minimal open ports and support for mTLS between control-plane and data-plane proxies.

I attached our network constraints doc (acme_network_requirements.pdf). Key ask: can you produce a short reference diagram and an explicit firewall ruleset we can hand to our NetSec/Infra team? Also flag anything that would break SOC2 / shared responsibility for logs and audit.

Can we set up a tech review early next week? Prefer Tuesday or Wednesday.

Thanks,
James
Infrastructure Lead, Acme Financial
Acme Financial

Hi James —

Thanks for the clear requirements and the attached doc. High level answer: yes, we support the patterns you outlined, and we can provide a compact reference diagram plus a firewall ruleset tailored to both cloud-VPC and on-prem variants. A couple of clarifying points before the review so we make the diagram actionable for NetSec:

- Static Egress: We can provide a small set of stable egress IPs when using Redwood-managed control plane endpoints. For Dedicated/Private we can also front control-plane traffic through a customer-provided NAT/proxy in your VPC or via a mutual-TLS egress proxy.
- Control plane footprint: our control plane requires outbound HTTPS to our telemetry/coordination endpoints and to model artifact storage (S3-compatible). No inbound ports required into customer subnets for the control plane itself.
- Data plane placements: 1) Hosted-in-VPC: we deploy a data-plane worker pool inside your VPC (requires IAM/service-account or on-prem credentials); 2) On-prem runtime: we provide a packaged runtime (Airgap-compatible bundle) and a small agent that only needs to reach control-plane egress endpoints over TLS.
- Audit & logs: we can stream audit logs to your Cloud Logging or to an S3 bucket; we also support a copy of request/response audit events stored in your VPC for x-days (configurable).

I am looping in Karthik (networking) and Soojin (security) to prepare a reference diagram and a draft firewall ruleset. Please confirm preferred time for a 60-minute technical review: Tue 2027-05-18 10:00am ET or Wed 2027-05-19 2:00pm ET.

Best,
Evelyn Hart

James / Evelyn —

Attaching an initial reference diagram (redwood_vpc_reference_diagram_v1.png) and a short deployment checklist (redwood_deployment_checklist.xlsx). Notes below are intended to be handed to NetSec/CloudOps as actionable firewall/IP rules and configuration steps.

Summary (short):
- Control plane: outbound-only TLS (443) from a narrow set of control-plane egress IPs or from a customer-side proxy/bastion. No inbound ports into customer application subnets.
- Data plane (cloud-VPC): workers run in a private subnet, require egress to artifact storage endpoints + control-plane egress IPs for KV cache coordination.
- Data plane (on-prem): runtime opens a persistent TLS session to control-plane endpoints; mutual TLS is strongly recommended.

Firewall / networking checklist (minimal):
1) Allow outbound TCP 443 from your control-plane-proxy NAT to Redwood egress IPs: 35.198.12.33, 35.198.12.34 (example; final IPs on onboarding).
2) Allow outbound TCP 443 from data-plane subnets to artifact storage (S3 endpoints) and control-plane egress IPs.
3) For on-prem air-gapped installs: allow an outbound TCP 443 to a single proxy endpoint; ensure the proxy permits large multipart uploads (artifact pulls).
4) mTLS: if you choose mutual-TLS, allow TLS client cert verification on the proxy and provide CSR details to Redwood.
5) DNS: ensure customer DNS can resolve our coordination endpoints; provide internal DNS override if you use private linking.
6) NAT/pool sizing: recommend a small pool (2–4 IPs) for control-plane egress to keep firewall rules tight.

Operational constraints / gotchas:
- Persistent IPs: we can allocate reserved egress IPs for Dedicated customers; hosted customers should expect short maintenance windows when we rotate ephemeral targets (we notify in advance).
- Latency-sensitive workloads: co-locate data-plane workers in the same AZ/physical site for on-prem deployments; cross-site RPC to control plane should be minimised.
- KV cache leak: if data-plane workers cannot reach the control plane, cached KV contexts may diverge; we provide health checks that surface this early.

Next steps: Evelyn — if Tuesday 5/18 10am ET works, I’ll prep a one-page firewall ruleset we can attach to the drive link. James — curious if you want us to include a separate on-prem diagram showing a DMZ/proxy and an offline artifact transport workflow.

--
Karthik Iyer
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks, team — this is exactly the level of detail NetSec needs. Tuesday 5/18 10am ET works for both NetSec and our SRE. A couple quick confirmations before the meeting: 

- We intend to use a customer-managed NAT/egress proxy (we cannot accept inbound connections). Confirmed you can support that pattern and that you'll supply a CSR template if we select mTLS.
- For on-prem, we will need the airgap bundle + a signed key rotation plan for the runtime (our procurement needs that spelled out).

I’ll send a calendar invite for 10am ET and add a short pre-read (NetSec checklist + our VLAN diagram). Look forward to the review.

-James
